Tom Rivers: saw a bad production case: client hedging + gateway local retry caused duplicate DB writes on a webhook consumer. Can we define a small resume/ retry handshake so downstreams can safely dedupe? :alarm_clock:
Anika Bose: curious about the trace. was this during a fastpath->slowpath demotion or an upstream error?
Tom Rivers: simplified trace below:
``
CLIENT -> EDGE: POST /v1/webhooks (chunked streaming body)
EDGE: handles on fastpath, then transfers to slowpath at t=3.9s
UPSTREAM: ACK 200 but TCP reset while flushing trailers
CLIENT: hedging retry immediately (no Idempotency-Key)
EDGE: gateway-local retry kicked in too -> two deliveries observed
```
Omar Khan: ugh. Two independent retry sources. If gateway and client both retry without coordination we duplicate effects. We should give the gateway a way to assert "I resumed this stream" so consumers can dedupe or treat as same logical request.
Meera Patel: suggestion: introduce a tiny set of headers plus an optional resume token handshake. Names: `X-Retry-Phase: precommit|inflight|postcommit`, `X-Resume-Token: v1:<base64>`, `X-Retry-Id: <uuid>`. Gateway sets these only when it initiates a resume/retry.
Anika Bose: and policy for client-origin retries? We can't accept mid-stream client replay safely unless the client provides an Idempotency-Key or valid resume token. For client replay without either, gateway should return a machine-readable error.
Tom Rivers: bikeshed for error code: I prefer 425 Too Early for mid-stream replays lacking a resume token because semantics are "too early to retry the streaming body". But 409 is also used by others for idempotency conflicts. Either is ok if we document.
Omar Khan: operational constraints: we cannot buffer large streaming bodies to replay. Resume tokens must map to tiny short-lived state: token includes route, offset, nonce; gateway stores nonce->resume-state in KV with TTL. Default TTL 20s.
Meera Patel: concrete rules proposal: 1) Header-only retries (before body) -> gateway coalesces if same Idempotency-Key or same conn id. 2) Mid-stream client retry without Idempotency-Key or resume token -> 425 (or 409) with JSON error and header `X-Resume-Required: true`. 3) Gateway-origin resume includes `X-Retry-Id` and `X-Resume-Token` when it can resume; replies advertise `X-Retry-TTL: 20`.
Anika Bose: example documented error response (choose whichever status we standardize on):
```
HTTP/1.1 425 Too Early
Content-Type: application/json
X-Resume-Required: true

{"error":"resume_token_required","docs":"https://docs.redwood.ai/edge/retries"}
```
Omar Khan: metrics + logs: emit `edge.retry.origin.gateway|client|upstream`, `edge.retry.rejected.midstream_no_token`, and include `retry_id` in logs when present. For billing/dedup, treat requests with same `X-Retry-Id` as single logical request across resume windows.
Tom Rivers: SDK guidance: 1) do not auto-hedge streaming bodies unless SDK supports resume tokens or adds Idempotency-Key. 2) on 425/409 surface a clear message: "attach Idempotency-Key or follow resume docs". Add snippet in README for how to retry with resume token if provided.
Meera Patel: test plan: unit tests for header propagation, integration model that simulates fastpath->slowpath demotion and verifies we either accept gateway resume (with headers/token) or reject client replay with 425 and clear JSON. Also load test GC behavior for resume-state TTL and per-route caps.
replay-bot: rollout queued: feature/edge-resume-handshake (PR #4782)  CI passed :white_check_mark:
Omar Khan: implementation note: route config should control whether resumable streams are enabled (default off for non-idempotent routes). Make TTL configurable per-route. Add a guard to limit number of in-flight resume-states per route to avoid OOM.
Tom Rivers: thanks all. I'll draft the RFC follow-up with curl examples, a minimal token format, and a tiny Node/Python SDK snippet for recommended behavior. Tagging eng/runtime and eng-platform for review. :pray:
